dish.title: Filipino Bistek Tagalog: Soy-Citrus Beef with Onion Rings and Rice
dish.description: Thin slices of sirloin marinated in soy sauce, calamansi or lemon juice, garlic, and black pepper, seared quickly and simmered in the marinade with soft white onion rings until glossy. Served over steamed rice.

recipe_version.title: Filipino Bistek Tagalog: Soy-Citrus Beef with Onion Rings and Rice
recipe_version.description: Thin slices of sirloin marinated in soy sauce, calamansi or lemon juice, garlic, and black pepper, seared quickly and simmered in the marinade with soft white onion rings until glossy. Served over steamed rice.

ingredients.name: beef sirloin
ingredients.preparation: very cold, sliced thin (1/4 inch) across the grain

ingredients.name: calamansi juice or fresh lemon juice
ingredients.display_name: calamansi juice or fresh lemon juice

steps.title: Slice and marinate
steps.body: Slice the very cold beef thin, 1/4 inch thick, across the grain. Toss with the soy sauce, citrus juice, garlic, pepper, and sugar in a bowl. Slice the onions into rings, rinse the rice, and slice the scallions.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice and 2 1/2 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high heat, cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes; rest covered 10 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.body: The beef marinates at room temperature for the 30 minutes the rice takes (overlap stated).

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.body: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Cook the onion rings until just softened, about 4 minutes, and transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.body: Raise the heat to high and add 1 tbsp oil. Lift the beef from the marinade (keep the marinade) and sear in two batches until browned at the edges, about 1 minute per side, adding the last 1 tbsp oil for the second batch.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.body: Return all the beef to the skillet with the reserved marinade and 1/3 cup water. Simmer over medium until glossy and slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Return the onions and toss 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Spoon the beef, onions, and sauce over the rice and scatter the scallions.

coverage_contribution: First Filipino beef dish (filipino-chicken-adobo and filipino-fish-sinigang are the others). Quick soy-citrus beef, a weeknight format.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with filipino-chicken-adobo: thin-sliced beef with citrus and onion rings, not vinegar-braised chicken. Compared with japanese-gyudon: seared steak slices in a sour soy-citrus sauce, not simmered beef in a sweet dashi-free broth. Compared with peruvian-lomo-saltado: no fries, tomatoes, or wok stir-fry.
not_duplicate_of: Not beef tapa (a cured breakfast cut).
